races.title: State House, District 39
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: James A. Roberson
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina House for District 39 (Wake County) since January 2021, appointed by Gov. Roy Cooper to replace Darren Jackson. Former two-term mayor of Knightdale. Education administrator, listed as senior dean and CCO of Wake Tech's Western Wake campus.
cands.gaps: We could not find where James Roberson was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no bills he sponsored (the sponsored-legislation list on his Ballotpedia page was empty), so we could not document specific actions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, guns or abortion. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any year, and his campaign site is brief and general. We found no stated positions from him on data centers or development, and no documented controversies. The endorsements we found were two online voter-guide recommendations, which we did not treat as notable. His campaign site mentions community-organization endorsements but does not list them.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State House member since January 2021 (appointed, then re-elected). Mayor of Knightdale, elected 2015 and 2019. Education administrator at Wake Technical Community College, listed as senior dean and CCO of the Western Wake campus.
qual.why: He has about five years of legislative service and six years as an elected local executive, plus an administrative career managing a college campus. He has no law or formal budget-policy career. Committee assignments were not counted.
qual.label: He has about five years of legislative service and six years as an elected local executive, plus an administrative career managing a college campus. He has no law or formal budget-policy career. Committee assignments were not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he will work to "ensure competitive teacher pay." It gives no percentage and says nothing about vouchers, charters or school choice.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he will work on legislation that supports public safety officers and prioritizes safe communities. It names no specific pay, pension or penalty proposals.

cands.name: Jorge Cordova
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina House District 39 in 2026. He advanced without a primary and lost the general election to incumbent Democrat James Roberson. No career or biographical details were found in the available record.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Jorge Cordova was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no information about his career, education or any office he has held. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and we found no campaign website, questionnaire or interview stating his positions on any issue. We found no documented actions in office, public statements on data centers or development, controversies, foreign ties or endorsements.
